question: Should ClawHub offer a public Verified or vetted-community request path for Spectyra and similar community plugins, or keep Official limited to staff-approved publishers?
rationale: This trust signal affects user install decisions for third-party executable plugins, and source code cannot choose the assurance criteria, reviewer authority, scope, expiry, revocation, or public wording safely.

options.title: Define general vetted-community policy first
options.body: Use the open RFC to settle criteria and semantics before granting Spectyra or any other community plugin a public trust signal.

options.title: Keep Official-only and document that boundary
options.body: Document that community plugins can rely on source, scan, provenance, and trusted-publishing evidence but cannot request Verified status today.

options.title: Perform a one-off Spectyra review
options.body: Maintainers could manually review Spectyra, but that risks creating precedent before the wider trust model is defined.

recommendation.title: Define general vetted-community policy first
recommendation.body: Use the open RFC to settle criteria and semantics before granting Spectyra or any other community plugin a public trust signal.

likelyOwner.reason: The current official publisher and package trust surfaces are attributed to this author in blame, so they are the best available routing owner for the policy boundary.
